messages:
maria (Support): Hey team, escalation from ACME: streaming response ends abruptly with an unterminated JSON array. Customer sees final payload like 'data: [ ...' and connection closes. finish_reason not present. They've hit this twice in prod today.

raj (SRE): Can you paste the exact client-observed tail from the stream and the request id/route?

maria (Support): Sure. Route: POST /v1/stream/generate model=gpt-large-stream, request-id: r-0a1b2c3d. Client tail (copied):

```
data: {"id":"resp_abc123","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"...and the final array starts here","index":0}]} 
data: [
```

Connection then closed by server, client parses and fails with SyntaxError. No finish_reason. Customer attached server-side request-id header: r-0a1b2c3d.

oliver (SDK): Does the customer use our JS SDK or raw fetch? Some SDKs buffer and then try to JSON.parse at end. If stream cuts at an array start that's fatal.

maria (Support): They use a custom Node fetch implementation in a background worker.

sophia (Client Eng): Repro attempt steps requested. Could you ask them to run a curl SSE client to confirm it's server-side? Example I ask them to run:

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -N \
  -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream/generate -d '{"model":"gpt-large-stream","prompt":"test break"}'
```

If curl shows same truncated output, it's likely server. If only their worker shows it, could be client-side abort.

maria (Support): They ran curl; attached output shows same trailing '[' line.

raj (SRE): Ok that points to server-side cutoff. Tim, any recent changes to keepalive or SSE framing on the runtime? :eyes:
\

tim (Eng - runtime): Not aware of intentional changes. Quick hypotheses: (1) auth token rotation triggered mid-stream close, (2) upstream proxy (fastly/nginx) hit a timeout and closed connection while a JSON array was being emitted, (3) a bug in the final flush path where the final sentinel/event isn't emitted under error code paths.

tim (Eng - runtime): Can we get the full ingress logs for r-0a1b2c3d and the backend worker logs? Also include any intermediate proxy response codes.

maria (Support): Pasted ingress log snippet from customer environment: `GET /_edge/stream 200 42ms r-0a1b2c3d` then TLS session ended. No 500. Customer says nothing in their proxy.

raj (SRE): I'll pull our side logs for that request id. Meanwhile, please ask customer to attempt a short workaround: enable automatic reconnect+resume on their client and treat incomplete JSON as retryable for now. Also test with a small prompt to see if deterministic.

oliver (SDK): Note for SDK users: add a parse-tolerant fallback: if final parse fails, attempt to append closing brackets/objects heuristically to avoid crashing UX. Not ideal but buys time.

dev-bot: Ticket created: #SUP-7242 streaming-incomplete-array-cutoff - assigned to eng-runtime.

maria (Support): Customer reported one more data point: when they switched to a different region the problem didn't reproduce. Could indicate an edge/proxy region issue.

tim (Eng - runtime): That is useful. Please collect the region header and the edge node id from their curl verbose output. Also capture raw TCP close behavior (RST vs FIN) if possible.

sophia (Client Eng): For repro we should add a test that streams an array start as the penultimate chunk and then intentionally close connection at the exact byte boundary. I can add a harness to simulate.

raj (SRE): Logged findings so far: curl reproduces -> server cut -> region-specific -> no 500 returned. Next steps: (1) correlate edge node logs for r-0a1b2c3d (2) run simulated close test in staging with edge enabled (3) check for recent proxy config change to idle timeouts around 30s.

maria (Support): I'll keep customer updated. They asked if this could be related to billing/auth rotation they saw earlier (401 on a separate request). Any likelihood?

tim (Eng - runtime): Unlikely if curl used same token and got truncated body with 200. But still include token rotation as a datapoint.

maria (Support): Thanks. I'll send their curl verbose output and edge node ids to eng-runtime and post back. :thumbsup:
